biggestGap: Nothing in the frame is nearer to the camera than the board — every piece of stone sits behind and above the ranks, so the outer quarters of frame are empty black void with flames floating in it; put colossal piers in the NEAR field standing hard against the left and right kerbs, close enough that they are cropped by both the top and the bottom of frame and physically overlap the front ranks, and kill the readable far termination behind them.
critiqueDetail: I called the film as panel B instantly and with high confidence, and I was right. This is a real improvement on round 1 and I want to be explicit about what now works: the masonry idiom has genuinely changed — the shafts and recesses read as smooth ordered carved stone rather than the crude coursed rubble of round 1, the palette and value structure are close (meanLitHue 219.3 vs 223.6, meanSaturation 0.334 vs 0.322, medianLuminance 0.122 vs 0.118), and the render is now byte-for-byte deterministic across two identical captures (same MD5), which clears round 1's blocking nondeterminism fail. The chamber is no longer a diorama in a warehouse. But it still does not ENCLOSE. In the film the architecture is a near-field object: colossal piers occupy the outer quarter of frame on both sides, are cut off by the top AND bottom of frame, stand physically forward of the front ranks, and behind the ranks more stone crowds in as an unresolvable dark mass with no legible termination. In our render every stone element lives BEHIND the pieces. The left and right thirds of frame are pure black with candle flames floating unsupported in them — no pier, no wall, no silhouette. All the arcade, string course and blind arcading that the rebuild added sits at the far end, where it resolves into a clean, symmetric, evenly-spaced ring of vertical shafts with crisp bright speculars along their edges, and a single fat column parked dead on the board's axis at the vanishing point catching the brightest architectural highlight in the frame. That colonnade announces exactly where the room ends and how big it is — about 20 m, and the shafts read at only two or three pawn-heights, so the hall is not cathedral scale. The film's far end is a dark curved unreadable mass; ours is a legible back wall. There is also a hard modelling artifact in the top-left corner: a dead-straight faceted black polygon edge runs diagonally from roughly (200,0) to (85,250), and outside it you see through to a brighter grey coursed-block wall and a fluted pier that should not be visible. It is not a vignette — it has a low-poly silhouette and it is asymmetric, present on the left only. In a 4K film frame that is an unshippable geometry leak. The metrics corroborate the enclosure diagnosis precisely. The film's detailByBand is nearly flat (0.02014 / 0.02098 / 0.02019); ours is (0.01139 / 0.03244 / 0.02578). detailTotal is close (0.0231 vs 0.0204) but the shape is wrong in the one band that matters here: coarse-scale edge energy is 0.01139 against 0.02014, only 57 percent of the film's, which is the missing near-field mass measured directly — there are no big shapes cutting the frame. That deficit is compensated by mid-band energy 55 percent OVER reference (0.03244 vs 0.02098), i.e. the repeating shaft ribbing and recess striping of the far arcade doing the work that colossal piers should be doing. gradientAnisotropy 1.247 vs 1.462 says the same thing from the other side: the film has stronger directional structure because it is dominated by huge vertical piers, ours is more isotropic fine detail. fracDeepShadow 0.0706 vs 0.1061 means we still do not reach the true blacks that let the film hide its boundaries — but that is now a secondary consequence of having a lit, readable back wall rather than an unresolved void.
metrics: letterbox: reference cropped 1080 -> 808 rows (274 rows of bars stripped), render 804 rows uncropped. medianLuminance 0.1216 vs 0.1176 (+0.004); meanSaturation 0.3335 vs 0.3220 (+0.0115); meanLitHueDeg 219.3 vs 223.6 (-4.3); fracDeepShadow 0.0706 vs 0.1061 (-0.0355); fracShadow 0.4919 vs 0.5098 (-0.0179); fracBlown 0.0092 vs 0.0065 (+0.0027); histogramEntropy 6.751 vs 6.894 (-0.143); warmFraction 0.1417 vs 0.1390 (+0.0027); coolFraction 0.5248 vs 0.4335 (+0.0913); detailTotal 0.02313 vs 0.02036 (+0.0028); detailByBand 0.01139/0.03244/0.02578 vs 0.02014/0.02098/0.02019 — reference nearly FLAT, render coarse band only 57% of reference and mid band 155% of reference; gradientAnisotropy 1.247 vs 1.462 (-0.215). Determinism PASS: two captures at t=3 are byte-identical (md5 164c4e11886d0190450d76d5b95289ed).

history.gap: No massive piers enclosing the board — the outer thirds of frame are empty floor and the whole room is visible at once, so it reads as a diorama in a warehouse instead of a cathedral-scale hall. Masonry is crude coursed block with heavy mortar rather than smooth carved Gothic. Render is also nondeterministic (85% of pixels differ between identical captures).

Called panel B as the film, high confidence, correct. Masonry idiom and determinism are genuinely fixed and the palette is close, but all stone still sits BEHIND the ranks: the outer quarters of frame are empty black with flames floating in them, and the far arcade resolves into a symmetric brightly-rim-lit colonnade with a column on the vanishing point that tells you exactly where the room ends. Coarse-band detail 0.01139 vs 0.02014 is the missing near-field mass measured directly. Also a hard faceted black polygon geometry leak in the top-left corner exposing a brighter coursed-block wall behind it.
